findings:
🟠 [inv1-quoted-value-empty-capture] MUST-FIX In hooks/tests/test-identity-guard.test.sh the repaired pattern `/['"]?user\.email=([^\s"';|&,\]\)]*)/g` stops at a quote placed after the `=`, so `git -c user.email="real@owner.com" commit` (or the single-quoted value form) emits a record with an EMPTY email. `is_test_identity_email ''` returns 0, so the line passes silently. Impact: a listed inventory syntax (`-c user.email=`) in its common value-quoted spelling lets a non-G2 address through KR5 with no failure, and any fixture written that way was never converted. Smallest remediation: give the value the same three alternatives the sibling patterns use, e.g. `/['"]?user\.email=(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)'|([^\s"';|&,\]\)]*))/g`, and add a `git -c user.email="valq-scan@github.com"` line plus assertion to the existing scanner self-test. Then re-run the suite and convert anything newly reported to `@example.invalid`.
🟠 [inv1-other-at-address-missing] MUST-FIX The row requires "any other `@`-address in a git-invoking test fails the inventory with file:line", but inventory one only judges records emitted by the six syntax regexes; there is no catch-all pass. Impact: identity spellings outside those regexes (e.g. `git commit --author="A <real@corp.com>"`, `git config --local user.email real@corp.com`) in a git-invoking `*.test.sh` pass the inventory unreported. Smallest remediation: for each `hooks/tests/*.test.sh` matching the inventory-two git-invoking grep, scan each line for an email-shaped token (`[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+`), skip `$`-expansions, and `fail "…file:line email"` unless `is_declared_control` or `is_test_identity_email` accepts it; convert newly reported fixtures to `@example.invalid`.
🔵 [inv2-subshell-git-detection] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The inventory-two detector `(^|[[:space:];|&])git[[:space:]]` does not match a file whose only git calls are written `$(git …)`. No concrete missed file is shown in the diff, so this is excluded as optional hardening (add `(` to the leading class).
